title: STRAIT OF HORMUZ — EXECUTIVE SITREP

sections.heading: STRATEGIC OVERVIEW
bullets: Connects Persian Gulf to Gulf of Oman; ~21 mi wide at narrowest navigable point.
~20-21 MBPD crude/condensate transits (~20-21% of global petroleum traded daily).
World's single largest LNG chokepoint; Qatar, UAE, and Kuwait primary exporters.
Closure or sustained disruption triggers immediate global energy price shock; no viable alternative route for Gulf producers at comparable volume.
Key importers at risk: China, India, Japan, South Korea, EU states.

sections.heading: OPERATIONAL ENVIRONMENT
bullets: IRAN (IRGCN/IRIN): Maintains fast-attack craft, submarine capability (Kilo-class), anti-ship missiles (Noor/Qader), and mine warfare assets. Routinely conducts freedom-of-navigation harassment operations.

U.S. 5th FLEET (Bahrain): Standing presence of carrier strike group (rotational), destroyers, Coast Guard cutters, and P-8 maritime patrol aircraft. Operates Combined Maritime Forces (CMF) with 40+ partner nations.
GCC: Saudi, UAE, and Bahraini naval assets patrol southern approaches. Saudi Arabia maintains Abqaiq-Yanbu pipeline bypass (~5 MBPD capacity) as partial contingency.
Standing Rules: International Recommended Transit Corridor (IRTC) observed; convoy procedures activated in elevated-threat periods.

War-risk insurance premiums spike 0.1%-0.5%+ of hull value during escalation; can reach 2%+ during acute crises. Lloyd's/JWC Listed Area — 7-day voyage notice required.
LNG re-routing via Cape of Good Hope adds ~10-14 days; vessels may deactivate AIS transponders in elevated-threat periods.

sections.heading: 72-HOUR WATCHPOINTS
bullets: IRGCN vessel surge or abnormal positioning near shipping lanes or offshore platforms.
Any seizure, boarding, or harassment of commercial vessel — escalation ladder trigger.
Iranian leadership statement signaling closure threat or retaliatory mining.
U.S./coalition carrier strike group repositioning or force posture change.
Brent price movement >5% from current $76.49/bbl — signals market pricing of disruption risk.
UN Security Council session, U.S. Treasury sanctions announcement, or JCPOA-related statement.
Israeli or GCC military activity with potential Iranian reciprocal response through maritime proxy.
